transcript.text: There's water all over the kitchen floor coming from under my Beko washing machine and its gone under the units to where the plug is, the machine is still going. What do I do?

Water near the plug or socket is dangerous. Please don't touch the plug, socket or machine if they or your hands are wet. If you can do it safely, switch off the circuit at the consumer unit (fuse box), keep away from the water, and don't use the machine again until a qualified electrician or appliance engineer has checked it. Stop using the machine immediately and switch it off at the wall before you go any further. Water has reached your plug socket, so this is a serious electrical hazard that must be inspected by a qualified engineer before the appliance can ever be used again. The leak could come from several places like the door seal, inlet hoses, or the pump filter, but we cannot safely diagnose it while it is running. Once it is safe to do so, check if the small pump filter cap at the bottom front is loose or cracked, as this is a common source of leaks.
ok the consumer unit is in the hall and the floor's dry there so I can switch it off from there. I'm standing in socks on the wet floor right now tho, should I get off it first?

Yes, get off the wet floor immediately to avoid any risk of electric shock before you go to switch it off at the consumer unit. A leak underneath your Beko could be caused by several things, such as a loose pump filter cap or a split hose, but we cannot safely diagnose it while it is still running. Once you have switched off the power and ensured the machine is safe, check if the small pump filter cap at the bottom front is loose or cracked, as this is a common source of leaks. Please do not attempt to use the appliance again until a qualified engineer has inspected it for electrical safety.
ok I've got off the wet floor and switched it off at the consumer unit in the hall. the water's mostly coming from the front under the door. what do I do now?

The water reaching your plug socket is a serious electrical hazard, so this appliance must not be used again until a qualified engineer has checked it for safety. Since the leak is coming from under the door and the machine was running while it happened, it could be caused by something like a loose pump filter cap or a split hose. Please check if the small pump filter cap at the bottom front of your Beko is loose or cracked, as this is a common source of leaks. To help us identify the correct parts, please find the model number on a sticker inside the door rim or on the back of the door.
[Panel: "To check a suitable replacement — Enter your model number below. Once we have the model I can check whether a suitable replacement is available. It's usually on a sticker inside the door or around the frame, or on the back of the appliance."]
ok the pump filter cap is tight and it's dry behind the flap. the model number on the label is WTK72041W. the water's still mostly at the front under the door tho, what now?

Water has reached your plug socket, so this appliance must not be used again until a qualified engineer has checked it for electrical safety. Since the leak is coming from under the door and the pump filter cap was dry and tight, the most likely cause is that something like a coin or hairpin is trapped in the rubber door seal folds. Please open the door and look all the way round the bottom of the rubber seal to see if there is any debris holding it open or causing a split.

ok the machine's still full of water, I can't pull it out on my own. I opened the door and there's a small split in the bottom fold of the rubber seal, with an underwire from a bra stuck next to it. is that the leak?

[Heading: Likely cause: door seal]
Yes, that split in the rubber seal with the underwire stuck next to it is very likely the cause of the leak onto your kitchen floor. Because water has reached your plug socket and gone under the units, this appliance must not be used again until a qualified engineer has checked it for electrical safety. You can remove the underwire carefully now that the machine is switched off at the consumer unit in the hall to stop any further tearing of the seal. A matching door seal part for your Beko WTK72041W is shown below; please check the listing matches your model exactly before ordering. If you are not comfortable replacing the seal yourself, or if the split looks extensive, it may be better to call in an engineer to ensure the repair is done safely and correctly.
